title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build a research-led academic career in aviation and airport studies through publications, teaching, funded research, supervision, academic service and eventually departmental leadership.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes the student begins or is in the first year of the selected Ph.D. in 2026. The goal is to emerge with a defensible research niche, peer-reviewed publications, teaching experience, conference visibility and a record of funded/project research.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Complete the Ph.D., establish a research niche, publish, present at conferences and build supervised-teaching experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Become an independent aviation/airport researcher and qualify for faculty positions through publications, teaching and research impact.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior faculty roles, lead research projects, supervise doctoral researchers and build institutional/industry partnerships.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become a recognised academic leader through research programmes, international collaboration, policy engagement and academic administration.

2040–2046: Professor → Programme Chair / Research Centre Director / Dean-level academic leadership

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

items.text: Air transport demand and network modelling

blocks.text: The professor-track objective should be more than reaching a title. Build a recognisable research programme with doctoral students, external funding, high-quality publications, international collaborators and industry/government partnerships. The strongest academic profile will connect aviation theory to real airport and air-transport problems while maintaining methodological credibility.
